knowledge-base.overview: Language-specific idioms, guardrails, and patterns for Kotlin 1.9+. Loaded automatically when agents work on .kt or .kts files. Covers null safety, coroutines with structured concurrency, data classes, sealed interfaces, scope functions, value classes, and testing with JUnit 5 and MockK. Applies to JVM 17+, Android, and server-side Kotlin.

core-principles.principle: Leverage the type system to eliminate null pointer exceptions at compile time. Nullable types only at API boundaries.
Use data classes, scope functions, and destructuring to reduce boilerplate without sacrificing readability.
Structured concurrency with coroutines, not raw threads. GlobalScope is forbidden in production.
Prefer `val` over `var`. Prefer read-only collections (`List`, `Map`, `Set`) over mutable variants.
Write idiomatic Kotlin while maintaining clean Java interop boundaries where required.

guardrail.rule: Never use the not-null assertion operator `!!` in production code. It throws KotlinNullPointerException with no useful context.
guardrail.bad: val length = name!!.length // crashes at runtime with no useful message

guardrail.rule: Never use GlobalScope in production code. It leaks coroutines and bypasses structured concurrency lifecycle management.
guardrail.bad: GlobalScope.launch { fetchData() } // unstructured, leaks on cancellation

guardrail.rule: Never swallow CancellationException. Always rethrow it. Catching CancellationException prevents coroutine cancellation from propagating correctly.
Use withContext(Dispatchers.IO) for blocking I/O inside coroutines. Never call blocking operations on the default dispatcher.
Prefer `val` over `var`. Mutable state must be justified. Immutable bindings prevent accidental reassignment and make data flow explicit.
guardrail.bad: var count = 0 var result = fetchUser(id) // 'result' never reassigned — should be val
guardrail.good: val count = items.size val result = fetchUser(id)

guardrail.rule: Use `requireNotNull()` or `checkNotNull()` with descriptive messages instead of `!!`. These throw IllegalArgumentException / IllegalStateException with useful context.
guardrail.good: val userId = requireNotNull(input.userId) { "userId is required in CreateUserRequest" } val session = checkNotNull(context.session) { "Session must be initialized before calling process()" }

guardrail.rule: Set timeouts on all external calls using withTimeout or withTimeoutOrNull. Unbound external calls can block coroutine dispatchers indefinitely.
Keep extension functions in dedicated files per type (StringExtensions.kt, DateExtensions.kt). Do not add extensions to Any or other overly generic types.
guardrail.bad: fun Any.toJson(): String = ... // too generic — pollutes all types

guardrail.rule: Run `ktlint` and `detekt` before every commit. These are non-optional. ktlint enforces formatting; detekt catches complexity, code smells, and unsafe casts.
guardrail.note: Configure via `build.gradle.kts` plugins block; see Tooling section for commands.

guardrail.rule: Nullable types belong only at API boundaries (deserialization, Java interop). Internal Kotlin code should be non-nullable wherever possible.
guardrail.bad: data class User(val name: String?, val email: String?) // why nullable internally?
guardrail.good: data class User(val name: String, val email: String) // validate at boundary before construction

guardrail.rule: Prefer read-only collection interfaces (List, Map, Set) in function signatures and data classes. Return mutable collections only when the caller must mutate.

directory.purpose: Business logic, entities, use cases — zero framework dependencies (pure Kotlin)
Data classes, sealed classes, value classes
Data layer — implements domain repository interfaces
API clients, DTOs for external services
UI controllers or API endpoint handlers

project-structure.note: domain/ has zero external dependencies. data/ depends on domain/. presentation/ depends on domain/ but never imports from data/ directly. No circular module dependencies.

pattern.name: Data Classes and Value Classes
pattern.description: Data classes for multi-field domain objects. Value classes for type-safe wrappers with zero runtime overhead (JVM inlining).

pattern.name: Sealed Interfaces for Result Types
pattern.context: Domain operations that can succeed or fail in known ways
pattern.description: Sealed interfaces model closed outcome hierarchies. when expressions are exhaustive — compiler enforces all cases are handled.

pattern.name: Scope Functions
pattern.context: Object configuration, nullable transforms, side effects
pattern.description: Use the right scope function for the right job. apply for configuration, also for side effects, let for nullable transforms.

pattern.name: Scope Functions Quick Reference
pattern.description: Reference table for let, run, with, apply, also.
pattern.example: | Function | Context | Returns | Primary use | |----------|---------|-------------|-------------------------------------| | let | it | Lambda result| Nullable transforms, scoped vars | | run | this | Lambda result| Compute value using object context | | with | this | Lambda result| Operate on non-null object | | apply | this | Object itself| Configure/build an object | | also | it | Object itself| Side effects (logging, events) |

pattern.name: Structured Concurrency
pattern.context: Any concurrent or parallel async work
pattern.description: Always bound coroutines to a scope. Use async/await for parallel work. supervisorScope when child failures must not cancel siblings.

testing.framework: JUnit 5 with MockK (Kotlin-idiomatic mocking, coroutine support) and AssertJ

rules.rule: Test files: `*Test.kt` under `src/test/kotlin/` — mirror source package structure
Use MockK for mocking (not Mockito — MockK handles suspend functions natively)
Use `runTest` from `kotlinx-coroutines-test` for all suspend function tests
Use `@ParameterizedTest` with `@MethodSource` for table-driven test cases
Coverage target: 80% business logic, 60% overall (enforced via Kover)

quick-reference.item: Forbidden in production — use ?., ?:, requireNotNull(), checkNotNull()
Forbidden — use coroutineScope{} or supervisorScope{} for structured concurrency
Always rethrow — never swallow in a catch(Exception) block
Required for all blocking I/O inside coroutines
Default to val; var requires justification
Only at API boundaries (deserialization, Java interop); internal code non-nullable
Use for multi-field domain objects; value class for type-safe single-value wrappers
Use for closed outcome hierarchies; enables exhaustive when expressions
In dedicated files per receiver type; never on Any
Return List/Map/Set (read-only); MutableList only when caller must mutate
MockK for mocking (not Mockito); runTest for suspend functions; coEvery/coVerify for coroutine mocks
ktlint + detekt mandatory before every commit
